title: micro-suggestion-rail-experimental-prd-scratch
content:
Quick brain-dump / rolling PRD sketch for a lightweight "micro suggestion" rail that surfaces short, actionable suggestions during an ongoing conversation. Meant to be low-cost, low-latency, and easily toggled by product teams.

Context / motivation:
- Customers building assistants want tiny, contextual prompts (1-6 tokens worth of guidance) that shorten flows (e.g., recommend follow-ups, quick clarifications, or synthesis snippets).
- Existing approaches (full-turn suggestions, separate UI panels) are heavier: more latency, more tokens, and more UX friction.
- Hypothesis: a thin suggestion rail computed from the session context and recent AI outputs can increase successful completions (task success / conversion) while adding negligible cost if inference is bounded and cached.

Problem statement:
- Need: fast per-turn suggestions that feel instantaneous and relevant, with control over cost and privacy.
- Constraints: must not increase median user-visible latency by >50ms; token budget per suggestion <= 12 tokens; allow per-customer opt-in and per-route config.

Proposal summary:
- Micro-suggestion rail: a side-channel endpoint that returns 0-3 short suggestions for the current conversation turn. Suggestions are served from a lightweight model variant / heuristic ensemble, optionally backed by cached prompts.
- API shape: POST /v1/suggestions?route=chat-turn returns suggestions with scores and origin tags (model/heuristic/cache).
- Modes: "local-heuristic", "compact-model" (small quantized LLM), "cached-history" fallback.

User personas:
- Product manager (PM): wants to experiment with suggestions to boost feature completion.
- Developer integrating Redwood API: needs a simple call and predictable cost.
- Privacy-sensitive enterprise customer: requires that suggestion generation respects session retention and KMS rules.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I can enable micro-suggestions for a route and set token/cost caps so the feature is safe to trial.
- As a developer, I can call the suggestions endpoint in parallel with the primary generation call and display suggestions when they arrive.
- As a customer admin, I can restrict suggestion generation to on-prem/private deployments or disable certain heuristics (e.g., proprietary data use).

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Latency: 95th-percentile suggestion return time <= 120ms when compact-model is used and cache miss is rare.
- Cost: average extra tokens billed per session <= 10 tokens (target 4–6 tokens).
- Quality: suggestions judged relevant in >60% of sampled QA sessions (A/B).
- Business: +5% lift in target completion metric in a 2-week canary with power-user cohort.

Technical design notes:
- Suggestion generator options:
  - Heuristic extractor: regex + entity templates + last-turn trigram compression (zero-cost, deterministic).
  - Compact model: 1.5B-3B quantized variant with tuned prompt that outputs 1-3 short suggestions, separated by ||. Prefer sparse attention kernels.
  - Re-ranking: very cheap scoring model that ranks suggestions by predicted usefulness using lightweight features (recency, token overlap).
- Caching: key = (route, last_n_tokens_hash, persona_tag). Cache TTL short (30s) to cover rapid UX interactivity. Use prefix/KV cache in runtime to avoid repeated model hits during multi-device sessions.
- API semantics: suggestions are advisory only; they may include a "confidence" float and an "origin" enum (heuristic/model/cache). If origin=model, include a small integer model-id shorthand to map to model catalog.

Integration patterns:
- Parallel call: front-end fires suggestions call concurrently with primary generation. If suggestions arrive within N ms (configurable, default 150ms), show rail; otherwise hide.
- Server-side merge: backend can request suggestions and choose to embed one as a forced follow-up prompt (requires opt-in and more tokens).

Privacy & security considerations:
- For Hosted: mark suggestion calls in telemetry; provide a toggle to exclude suggestions from long-term telemetry/retention.
- For Dedicated/Private: allow suggestion generation to be executed in-customer environment or flagged to avoid external re-ranking.
- Avoid storing raw suggestions in logs by default; store hashes for debugging.

Experimentation plan:
- Phase A (internal): implement heuristic + UI stub. Measure latency overhead, cache hit-rate. Quick label set for relevance sampling.
- Phase B (small beta): enable compact-model on one route for 5% of traffic. A/B test lift on completion metric.
- Phase C (rollout): expose console controls (enable, cap tokens, choose origin priority), provide sample prompts and recommended heuristics.

Metrics to capture (frontend + backend):
- suggestion_request_rate, suggestion_response_latency_ms_p95, suggestion_cache_hit_rate
- avg_extra_tokens_per_session, suggestions_shown_rate, suggestion_click_through_rate, downstream_completion_conversion_delta

Operational considerations / SLOs:
- Hard cap: if suggestion endpoint is overloaded, return empty suggestions rather than delay primary generation.
- Observability: surface per-route suggestion counts, distribution of origins, top-k suggestion texts (hashed) for sampling.

Rollout & console UX ideas:
- Quick toggles in Console: "enable micro-suggestions", "token cap per session", "prefer heuristics over model"
- Inline preview with sample contexts + what suggestions would look like (simulated).

Open questions / parking lot items:
- Should suggestions be generated synchronously in the same model invocation (hot path) or always via side-channel? (tradeoff: simplicity vs. blast radius)
- Policy: do suggestions need content filters different from primary generation? e.g., do-we-block certain suggestion types?
- Cost accounting: should suggestions be charged to the same route as primary request or to a separate suggestions SKU?
- UX: acceptable number of suggestions (1 vs 3) by product vertical (search vs. chat vs. task).

Immediate TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype heuristic extractor (eta: 2d)
- [ ] Spike compact-model latency on ded-1 GPU (eta: 1w)
- [ ] Draft Console controls mockups with UX (Lena/AvA)
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and link experiments (JIRA-4821 created)

Notes to self:
- Keep default conservative: heuristics first, cache second, model third.
- Try to reuse existing KV prefix caching infra; talk to Sana/Ivana about eviction semantics.
- Watch out for accidental privacy leaks in suggestion caching.

Snippets / prompt sketches (for compact-model):
- System: "You are a terse suggestion generator. From the user conversation below, output up to 3 short suggestions (each <= 12 tokens) separated by '||'. Prioritize follow-up questions and single-line actions. Do not include markup.
Conversation: {last_turns}
Output:"

End of scratch. Will iterate when I have microbench numbers.

-- Thiago
